summary: Arthur Maurice Hocart (1883–1939) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Elizabeth College and Exeter College, he held posts at Oxford, the Archaeological Commission in Sri Lanka (1921–1929), University College London (1931–1934), and Cairo University (1934).
Arthur Philip McKeown works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Harvard University, where he studied under Parimal G. Patil, Pari Sangye, and Diana L. Eck.

Philosopher Arthur Schopenhauer (1788–1860) studied at Ernestinum Gotha, Göttingen, Humboldt University of Berlin under Schleiermacher, Boeckh, and Wolf, and Jena (Doktortitel, ~1813). He also attended Friedrich Majer's lectures and held a Dozentur at Berlin in 1820.

Indologist Arthur Venis (1857–1918) studied at Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Education Service, worked as professor and principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University between 1881 and 1914, and became professor at Allahabad in 1914.

Arthur Waley (1889–1966) worked in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Rugby School and King's College, Cambridge, he served at the British Museum (1913–1929) and later held an honorary lectureship at SOAS (1948).

Arthur Wilhelm Gleye (1867–1937) was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Tartu under Leo Meyer (~1888–1893). He later served as a lecturer of German at Tomsk State University from 1901 to 1921.

Indologist Arthur William Ryder (1877–1938) studied at Harvard, Berlin, and Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, Charles Rockwell Lanman, and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He taught at Harvard before serving as professor at the University of California from ~1906 to 1938.
Arthur Woollgar Verrall (1851–1912) was an academic who studied at Wellington College (~1864–1869) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1869–1873). He later taught Robert Alexander Neil.

Arti Dhand (born 1966) specializes in religious studies and Indology. She studied at McGill University and the University of Calgary, and she became an associate professor in the Department for the Study of Religion at the University of Toronto around 2002.

Artur Kibat (1878–1960) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Königsberg under Adalbert Bezzenberger, completing his Ph.D. in 1904, and worked as a teacher at Oberrealschule Wilhelmshaven in 1910.
Aruna Haldar (born 1918) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She studied under Kedarnath Ojha and Girindrasekhar Bose, and she later served as a teacher at Patna University.

Indologist Arunoday Natvarlal Jani (1921–2003) earned a PhD at the University of Mumbai under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt. He served as professor and department head at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and directed the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (1975–1981).

Arvind Sharma (born 1940) specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Allahabad, Syracuse, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University, he taught at Queensland and Sydney before taking the Birks Chair in Comparative Religion at McGill in 1994.

Aryadeva (200–250) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Nagarjuna and Shakyamitra. He taught numerous students, including Shakyamitra and Candrakīrti, and held an affiliation with the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning.
Aryendra Sharma worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his doctoral studies under Walther Wüst by 1939 and was attested as director at Osmania University in 1969.

Asanga Tilakaratne (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at the University of Peradeniya and University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, he held professorships at the University of Kelaniya, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Colombo.
Asatoshi Kamiya is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. from Komazawa University (attested 1973) and served as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin High School (attested 1978).

Aschwin Lippe (1914–1988) worked in Indology, Sinology, and archaeology. He earned a Ph.D. from Humboldt University of Berlin (1942), worked as a curator at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (1949–1973), and served as curator at the University of Paris in 1980.

Asen Balikci (1929–2019) worked in history and archaeology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University (1956) and held positions at the Canadian Museum of History, National Museum of Canada, and Université de Montréal (1963–1993).

Ashok Aklujkar (born 1941) is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. Educated at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, he taught in the Department of Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia (1969–2006).
